confirmed.statement: S2 explicitly reports random assignment of participants to an AI-content treatment group or a control group; this supports randomized=yes and unit=individual.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph beginning "Second, Study 2 evaluates human-written emails".

confirmed.statement: S2 assigned AI-generated material to assist participants in writing their own business emails; the manipulation concerned assistance during production, and separate evaluators subsequently rated the emails.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph, assignment sentence and email-quality evaluation sentences.

confirmed.statement: S2 used separate groups: 240 participants received an AI-generated response and 240 other participants did not. This supports structure=between; condition-order randomization is not applicable.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Research motivation and overview, final paragraph, sentences beginning "In Study 2, 240 participants" and "For the treated participants".

confirmed.statement: The S2 control was instructed to write the email as in a typical work setting without any AI-generated content for assistance, matching the form's no-AI comparison.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph, control-group instruction in the random-assignment sentence.

confirmed.statement: S2 reused ChatGPT-4 responses from Study 1; the limitations explicitly identify the generator as the large language model GPT-4, supporting the generative_ai classification.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Research motivation and overview, final paragraph; p. 2, Methods, Study 1 paragraph; p. 9, Limitations, second limitation.

confirmed.statement: AI responses appeared as text directly below the task instruction and were pre-generated, supporting ideas_supplied and availability during email writing.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Research motivation and overview, final paragraph; p. 9, Limitations, first limitation.

confirmed.statement: The randomized contrast was AI assistance within the language groups; the paper describes participants as proficient in English, Arabic, or Chinese and does not report random assignment of language.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph; p. 3, Statistical analysis, specification (1) and the explanation of within-language average treatment effects.

confirmed.statement: The paper calls S2 preregistered and supplies the OSF address https://osf.io/u7s2g; the registration itself was not independently inspected.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 2 paragraph; p. 3, Methods continuation, paragraph beginning "SI Section A describes".

confirmed.statement: S1 evaluates ChatGPT-4 responses with human raters and is correctly distinguished from S2's randomized assignment of writing assistance.
confirmed.locator: Main PDF p. 2, Methods, Study 1 and Study 2 paragraphs.

summary: Study 2 explicitly randomly assigned people to supplied GPT-4 content or no AI-generated assistance for their own email writing, supporting criterion 1 and the form's between-person, ideas-supplied coding. No assignment-coding error was found after reading the complete main document; the separately linked supplement could not be retrieved because requests to PMC Open Access S3, Europe PMC, and the publisher were blocked.
